idea: HQC-5 produced wrong keys and ciphertexts on the device. The reference BITMASK macro uses 1UL, which is 32 bits on RV32, and HQC-5 shifts by 37.
change: override the macro in the suite's unit files; no upstream file changed
note: Correctness fix, not an optimization. Affects the reference code on any 32-bit target.

idea: Every product in HQC has one sparse operand (a few dozen set bits). The reference multiplies two dense polynomials with Karatsuba on 64-bit words, which is slow on RV32 and needs a work area of 18n bits. Shifting and XORing the dense operand once per set bit is far less work.
change: suites/hqc/pqc_suite/hqc_c3_pke.c with the inner loop in hqc_c3_mul.S
note: 375K cycles per product. Work area 2n bits instead of 18n. The assembly loop is 1.6x faster than the same loop in C. The secret positions choose memory addresses and shift counts: on this chip the on-device job ct-mul measures identical cycle counts for 24 supports including adversarial ones, but on a CPU with a data cache, or against power analysis, this leaks where the reference does not.

idea: The reference multiplies in GF(2^8) with table lookups or bit loops; the chip has a fast integer multiplier, so a carry-less product built from integer multiplications followed by a reduction avoids both.
checked: exhaustive comparison with the reference field multiplication

idea: The generic sponge absorbs and squeezes byte by byte with 64-bit shifts; working on words should save time on every hash.
note: About 10% off each hash call. The same change would help components/prims/fips202.c.

idea: The Hadamard transform and peak search of the reference decoder can be restructured for a 32-bit core.
checked: random words against the reference (8 rounds on the device, 200000 on the host)
official KAT (3 vectors per level on the device, 100 on the host) + fingerprint
note: Keygen 276.9 -> 5.52 ms, encaps 553.3 -> 11.46 ms; stack 66.1 -> 20.4 KB for decaps. Measured before the assembly Keccak was linked.

idea: The reference code needs 132 KB of stack for HQC-3 decapsulation and about 211 KB for HQC-5; a task stack is capped near 115 KB because the heap is split into regions of at most 128 KB.
change: HQC-3 reference runs in its own image (suite hqc3ref) on a static stack; HQC-5 reference is verified on the host only
note: The optimized HQC-5 needs 61.6 KB and runs on the device.
